title: Session orchestration: SDK patterns for fragmented tool invocations and progressive structured outputs (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: define and ship a set of language-specific example patterns and minimal interfaces that demonstrate session-oriented orchestration for progressive (streaming) model outputs + multi-step tool/function invocations. Focused outcomes: (1) a simple session token/cookie pattern for resuming incremental streaming, (2) an envelope framing recommendation for interop between TS/Py/Go SDKs, and (3) canonical examples that show tool calls returning structured JSON objects while preserving resumability and deterministic replay for evals.
background: Customers are asking for clear guidance on how to wire streaming LLM responses into multi-tool orchestration without losing ability to: checkpoint, resume mid-stream, and attach typed expectations for structured outputs. Existing demos show progressive outputs and tool calls separately; we need convergent examples that work cross-language and survive transient failures (connection drop, server failover) and model fallback scenarios.
decision_summary: We will adopt a minimal session envelope that includes: session_id, sequence_cursor, last_ack_token, and optional checkpoint metadata (hash of last committed structured object). For structured outputs we standardize on a small set of typed event names (partial_text, tool_call.request, tool_call.response, structured_object.commit, stream.end). Each SDK will expose a small SessionClient with: startSession(), resume(session_id), sendInput(), onEvent(callback) and a compact typed event enum. We decided against heavyweight binary framing or language-specific mutation APIs to keep cross-language surface small.
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs performance: adding session envelopes increases per-message bytes but greatly simplifies resume semantics and makes tooling deterministic (worth it for customer reliability).
Typed events vs freeform JSON: we pick a narrow event vocabulary + optional schema_uri for structured_object.commit to allow extensible validation without forcing full schema bundling in the SDK.

Sync ergonomics vs async streams: TypeScript SDK will provide both async iterator and callback hooks; Python will favour async iterator/generator + sync shim; Go will provide channel-based streaming and a context-aware resume API.
acceptance_criteria: TS/Py/Go example projects compile and run a demo that: starts a session, streams a partial response, triggers a tool_call.request event, receives tool_call.response with structured JSON, commits a structured_object and then resumes after simulated connection drop to continue streaming until stream.end.
SDK surface is less than 8 exported names per language for the core session + tooling helpers and documented in the README.

Integration tests cover resume semantics with at least two different model backends and a fallback scenario where primary model returns non-streamable error and runtime falls back to compatible model variant.
Design doc describing perf characteristics and an opt-in compressed framing is merged and reviewed by infra and security teams.
implementation_notes: TS: add src/session.ts exporting SessionClient and Event types; provide examples in examples/session-tooling/ts using fetch streaming and an async iterator wrapper.
Py: add redwood_sdk/session.py with SessionClient, provide sync wrapper with iterate_events() and async generator examples in examples/session-tooling/py.
Go: add sdk/session.go exposing SessionClient, Start/Resume with a channel-based event stream documented in examples/session-tooling/go.
Provide a canonical framing doc at docs/sdk/session-framing.md and include JSON Schema pointers for structured_object.commit events.
Create a small helper in runtime to emit last_ack_token for every confirmed commit; runtime change tracked in infra PR #7142.
notes: Prototype validated with internal sample app: messaging-bot that calls external search tool mid-stream and merges tool results into structured reply — metrics show resume adds ~1.5ms median per-message overhead.
Need to coordinate with console team to add session-level tracing IDs for per-route dashboards (PM: Lena Kovács).
Security: KMS handling unchanged; session envelope does not include secrets. We will add guidance for not embedding PII in checkpoint metadata.
